articles.title: New Simulations Connect the First Galaxies to the Universe We See Today
articles.description: In a recent study, researchers at the international MEGATRON project used some of the most detailed simulations of the early Universe to investigate how the first stars and galaxies formed.
articles.summary: The MEGATRON project's detailed simulations successfully connect the first galaxies to the present-day universe. This breakthrough advances our understanding of cosmic evolution over billions of years.

articles.title: The phoenix planet: Astronomers find a world reborn from its star's ashes
articles.description: Astronomers have discovered the first example of a second-generation planet orbiting a white dwarf, a world that appears to have formed from the remains of the dead star it now orbits.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Astronomers discover the first second-generation planet orbiting a white dwarf, representing a world reborn from stellar remnants. This extraordinary finding revolutionizes our understanding of planetary formation and longevity.

articles.title: NASA’s Roman telescope just opened its planet-hunting eye
articles.description: NASA’s Roman Space Telescope has demonstrated remarkable pointing stability and given its powerful planet-imaging coronagraph its first look at the cosmos. The telescope can already stay locked on a target with precision comparable to aiming a laser at a dime from about 150 miles away. Its coronagraph also captured stars in the Large Magellanic Cloud, confirming that the instrument can produce focused images.
articles.summary: NASA's Roman Space Telescope has demonstrated exceptional pointing stability and activated its powerful planet-imaging coronagraph. This landmark achievement brings the mission closer to discovering and characterizing exoplanets.

articles.title: First Direct Image of Protoplanet Swirling Surrounding Gas
articles.description: The formation and evolution of planets is the driving force behind both where and how we might find life beyond Earth. This complex and lengthy process first begins with a massive ball of gas and dust that swirls until it flattens into a disk, followed by roc…
articles.summary: Astronomers have captured the first direct image of a protoplanet surrounded by swirling gas, offering unprecedented insights into planetary formation. This discovery illuminates how planets develop and where habitable worlds might form.

articles.title: The Universe Is Full of Tiny Red Dots—and They’re One of Astronomy’s Biggest Discoveries in Decades
articles.description: A new type of object found in the early universe has puzzled astronomers for years, but they may finally have some answers.
articles.summary: Astronomers have identified a new class of mysterious objects in the early universe, solving a decade-long puzzle that represents one of the field's most significant discoveries.

articles.title: APOD: 2026 October 6 – A Complete Auroral Oval from SMILE
articles.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 6 – A… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss   APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. ESA, CAS, […]
articles.summary: SMILE satellite captures a complete auroral oval, offering unprecedented views of Earth's magnetic interaction with the solar wind. This represents a significant advancement in understanding auroral phenomena and space weather.

articles.title: A Journey to the Depths of Ancient Mars?
articles.description: Written by Alex Jones, Ph.D. candidate at Imperial College London Sept. 29, 2026 After spending the last six months exploring “Lac de Charmes,” a region of ancient rock beyond Jezero crater’s western rim, Perseverance has stumbled upon a vast field of light-toned rocks peppering the Martian surface.  Light-colored rocks are a strange sight on Mars, […]
articles.summary: Research explores the possibility of discovering subsurface water and ancient microbial life in Mars' deep past, expanding our understanding of the Red Planet's potential for past habitability.

articles.title: Suspected Second-generation Planet Solves NASA Hubble Cold Case
articles.description: New analysis of archival Hubble data points to the possibility of “dead” white dwarf stars hosting second-generation planetary systems.
articles.summary: Hubble Space Telescope archival data reveals evidence of second-generation planets orbiting white dwarf stars, opening new possibilities for understanding planetary formation and survival around stellar remnants.

articles.title: Webb captures commotion from nebula’s stellar jets
articles.description:
Image:
			Webb captures commotion from nebula’s stellar jets
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope captures stunning images of stellar jets and dynamic activity within a nebula, revealing the violent and creative processes of star formation in unprecedented detail.

articles.title: Science begins for Smile
articles.description: On 23 September, the European-Chinese Smile mission was declared ready to start revealing how Earth responds to the wind of charged particles from the Sun. This follows a busy in-space commissioning period since the spacecraft launched on 19 May and reached its target orbit for science operations on 20 June.
articles.summary: The European-Chinese SMILE mission begins its scientific observations, ready to investigate how Earth's magnetosphere responds to solar wind interactions. This collaborative effort marks a major milestone in space weather research.

articles.title: Galaxies in a cosmic house of mirrors
articles.description:
Image:
			
This NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope Picture of the Month features galaxies in great detail that have been warped and multiplied like they’ve stepped into a house of mirrors. The brilliant golden galaxies splashed across this image belong to a galaxy cluster called MACS J0454.1-0300. The orange galaxies concentrated on one side of the cluster are not actually part of the cluster and are much farther away from us.
MACS J0454.1-0300 is itself immensely distant: the light from these galaxies has been travelling to us for so long that we’re seeing the cluster as it was when the Universe was about 8 billion years old. While this galaxy cluster is a valuable scientific target in its own right, the real stars of this image are the galaxies that appear warped and stretched, like a painting that has been smeared by a giant hand.
The way these galaxies look is the result of gravitational lensing, in which the enormous mass of a foreground object such as a galaxy cluster bends and magnifies the light from a more distant object in the background. Gravitational lensing allows astronomers to observe galaxies, star clusters and even individual stars that are too far away for our telescopes to see under normal conditions. While the large, orange galaxies appear obviously distorted, look carefully at some of the small reddish background galaxies throughout this picture: even at the very edges of the frame, there are galaxies whose images have been bent into tiny arcs by MACS J0454.1-0300’s gravity.
The gravitationally lensed areas show multiple images of galaxies from when the Universe was young: a group of galaxies 2 billion years after the Big Bang, and a single galaxy just 800 million years old after the Big Bang. The galaxy group appears to be going through a merger, resulting in an enormous burst of star formation.
Astronomers have also identified individual bright ‘knots’ within the gravitationally lensed areas, corresponding to regions as small as 5 light-years across. These tiny clumps appear magnified by a factor of more than 300, in some cases.
A NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope image of this same cluster was released in 2014. Take a moment to compare the two images; the difference between them is dramatic. The new Webb image reveals hundreds of galaxies missing from the earlier image. These galaxies were there all along, but Webb is much more sensitive to their much redder light.
The data behind this image come from two observing programmes (#5058, PI: Furtak; #6882, PI: Fujimoto) that leverage the ability of massive galaxy clusters to bring distant objects into view.
[Image Description: A massive galaxy cluster, made of many golden elliptical galaxies with the largest, brightest one in the centre. Heavily distorted orange galaxies appear all around the cluster, the largest concentrated in a large arc around the cluster's centre; these are images of very distant galaxies, created by gravitational lensing. A few galaxies are large and bluish-white in colour; bright, nearby stars are the same colour.]
Release on esawebb.org
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope reveals galaxies in extraordinary detail through gravitational lensing, demonstrating the power of cosmic magnification to study distant galaxies and early universe formation.

articles.title: Successful Earth flyby improves Juice’s course to Jupiter
articles.description: The European Space Agency’s Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer (Juice) skimmed the very outer edge of Earth’s atmosphere on 28 September, using the gravity of our home planet to alter its route to Jupiter using very little fuel.
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's JUICE spacecraft successfully performs an Earth gravity assist maneuver, precisely adjusting its trajectory toward Jupiter and its fascinating icy moons. This demonstrates the success of complex interplanetary navigation.

articles.title: A Buried Volcano on the Moon Hints At An Ancient Lunar Dynamo
articles.description: Scientists know for certain the moon doesn’t currently have a magnetosphere. But they’ve been debating for decades about whether it ever did. Data from both Apollo samples and orbital scientific instruments have proven divisive, and so the debate still rages. But a new paper from researchers at ETH Zurich, DLR, and the Institute of Applied Geosciences hopes to resolve the debate once and for all - by definitively proving that the Moon did, indeed, once have a magnetic dynamo.
articles.summary: Scientists discover evidence of an ancient lunar magnetic field through analysis of a buried volcano on the Moon. This discovery provides new insights into the Moon's early history and geological evolution.

articles.title: Chandra X-ray Observatory Drops New View of our Galaxy’s Unruly Centre
articles.description: The core of the Milky Way is a dense, active, messy region, dominated by a supermassive black hole called Sagittarius A* (Sgr A*) hiding at the heart of the galaxy. But Sgr A* is only a supporting actor in this stunning new image from the Chandra X-ray Observatory.
articles.summary: The Chandra X-ray Observatory reveals a new perspective of the Milky Way's core and its supermassive black hole Sagittarius A*. This observation illuminates the dynamic processes at the heart of our galaxy.

articles.title: Neutrons, Rotating Black Holes, and a Galactic PeVatron at the Center of the Milky Way
articles.description: Supermassive black holes generate tremendous amounts of energy through their accretion disks and jets. But they can also generate energy through the magnetic Penrose process. A new study looks at how we might observe this process through multimessenger astronomy.
articles.summary: Research explores how supermassive black holes generate energy through accretion and jets, with new findings about high-energy particles at the Galactic Center. This study deepens our understanding of extreme cosmic phenomena.

articles.title: XRISM Makes First-Ever Detection of a Pulsar Feeding from a Companion's Stellar "Wind"
articles.description: Using data from the Japan-led XRISM observatory, astronomers have directly observed a giant star’s stellar wind captured by its compact companion (triggering X-ray flares) for the first time.
articles.summary: The XRISM observatory makes a groundbreaking detection of a pulsar capturing stellar wind from a companion star. This first-ever observation opens new avenues for understanding pulsar behavior and stellar interactions.

articles.title: This mysterious hole on the Moon may open into a giant cave
articles.description: NASA has selected the GIMLI project to investigate whether the Marius Hill Pit opens into a vast underground cave or lava tube. Using radar, seismic sensors, gravity measurements, and cameras, researchers will search beneath the lunar surface and estimate the size of any hidden void. Such caves could preserve clues to the Moon’s volcanic history and potentially provide protected shelters for future astronauts.
articles.summary: NASA's GIMLI project has been selected to investigate whether the Marius Hill Pit on the Moon opens into a vast underground cave or lava tube. This discovery could reveal hidden lunar geology and potential resources.

articles.title: Scientists find a surprising clue to why the universe’s expansion doesn’t add up
articles.description: Tiny magnetic fields created shortly after the Big Bang may help explain the long-running disagreement over how fast the universe is expanding. Detailed simulations show that these primordial fields could have changed the formation of hydrogen in the early universe, affecting the cosmic microwave background and the expansion rate inferred from it.
articles.summary: Scientists propose that tiny magnetic fields created shortly after the Big Bang may explain the long-running disagreement over the universe's expansion rate. This breakthrough could resolve one of cosmology's greatest puzzles.

articles.title: ESA’s Juice just used Earth as a slingshot to Jupiter
articles.description: ESA’s Juice spacecraft raced past Earth on September 28, using our planet’s gravity to dramatically reshape its path toward Jupiter without burning much fuel. The flyby changed its direction by 20 degrees and increased its speed by 3.5 km/s, while also giving scientists a rare chance to test its instruments on Earth and the Moon.
articles.summary: ESA's Juice spacecraft successfully used Earth's gravity as a slingshot on September 28 to reshape its trajectory toward Jupiter. This maneuver marks a critical milestone in the mission's journey to explore Jupiter's moons.

articles.title: Chang’e-6 lunar soil contains a surprising magnetic time capsule
articles.description: Scientists studying Chang’e-6 lunar soil have discovered a previously unknown magnetic mineral in natural Moon samples: a form of metallic iron called γ-Fe. Found inside tiny impact-glass particles, the nanoscale iron can preserve a stable magnetic signal, potentially acting like a microscopic fossil of the Moon’s long-lost magnetic field.
articles.summary: Scientists analyzing Chang'e-6 lunar samples have discovered a previously unknown magnetic mineral in Moon soil, revealing surprising insights into the Moon's magnetic history. This find expands our understanding of lunar geology.

articles.title: Powerful simulations reveal how the first stars changed the universe
articles.description: Ultra-detailed simulations are showing how the first stars lit up the dark Universe and seeded space with elements such as carbon, oxygen, and iron. The MEGATRON project could bridge JWST observations of the earliest galaxies with chemical clues preserved in ancient stars today.
articles.summary: Ultra-detailed simulations reveal how the first stars illuminated the early universe and seeded space with heavy elements necessary for life. This breakthrough helps explain the cosmic origins of matter itself.

articles.title: China's FAST telescope to advance with Phase II construction as project marks 10th anniversary
articles.description: The Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical Radio Telescope (FAST), known as the China's "Sky Eyes", will mark the 10th anniversary of its inauguration on September 25. Since its launch, the facility has achieved a series of landmark scientific and technologica…
articles.summary: China's FAST radio telescope, the world's largest single-aperture facility, advances to Phase II construction as it celebrates its 10th anniversary of groundbreaking astronomical observations.

articles.title: Η NASA ψάχνει για κρυφό γιγάντιο σπήλαιο κάτω από τη Σελήνη – Η «τρύπα» που μπορεί να κρύβει έναν τεράστιο υπόγειο κόσμο
articles.description: Ραντάρ, σεισμικοί αισθητήρες, βαρυόμετρο και κάμερες θα αναζητήσουν κάτω από την επιφάνεια της Σελήνης στοιχεία για έναν πιθανό τεράστιο υπόγειο σχηματισμό
articles.summary: NASA is searching for massive lunar caves beneath the Moon's surface using radar, seismic sensors, and cameras to explore potential underground habitats for future exploration.

articles.title: NASA spacecraft gains 3.5 km/s speed from Earth’s gravity assist without major engine burn
articles.description: On September 28, 2026, Juice, the Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer, accomplished a successful gravity assist flyby of Earth. This maneuver was pivotal in adjusting the spacecraft's trajectory and significantly boosting its speed without the need for extensive engin…
articles.summary: NASA's Juice spacecraft successfully completed a gravity assist maneuver around Earth on September 28, 2026, gaining 3.5 km/s velocity without requiring a major engine burn.

articles.title: NASA готовит новый класс космических миссий — телескоп PRIMA изучит далекую Вселенную
articles.description: NASA перевела миссию PRIMA (PRobe far-Infrared Mission for Astrophysics) на новый этап разработки, в рамках которого продолжатся проектирование аппарата и создание необходимых технологий.
articles.summary: NASA's PRIMA far-infrared mission telescope advances to a new development phase, positioning itself to study the distant universe and unlock mysteries of early cosmic structures.

articles.title: SpaceX's Starship Needs To Be Fully Operational By 2028 — Here's Why
articles.description: SpaceX has plenty left to test on Starship, from refueling to docking in orbit, and NASA is counting on it to finish in time for a much bigger assignment.
articles.summary: SpaceX's Starship must achieve full operational status by 2028 to support NASA's lunar missions, with remaining tests including orbital refueling and docking maneuvers.

articles.title: Curiosity Blog, Sols 5029-5035: Back in the Lab
articles.description: Written by Michelle Minitti, MAHLI Deputy Principal Investigator Earth planning date: Friday, Oct. 1, 2026 The majority of Curiosity plans involve mosaics from Mastcam and ChemCam, chemistry analyses from ChemCam and APXS, images from MAHLI and MARDI, and systematic measurements from REMS, RAD, and DAN. It is only when we stop to drill that we […]
articles.summary: NASA's Curiosity rover continues its scientific investigations on Mars, conducting laboratory analyses that advance our understanding of Martian geology and habitability. The rover remains productive in its extended mission on the Red Planet.

articles.title: NASA to Stream SpaceX Crew-12 Return, Splashdown Live
articles.description: NASA and SpaceX are targeting no earlier than 8:05 a.m. EDT, Wednesday, Oct. 7, for the undocking of the agency’s SpaceX Crew-12 mission from the International Space Station, pending weather conditions. An Oct. 7 undock puts NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev […]
articles.summary: NASA and SpaceX are preparing to stream the live return and splashdown of Crew-12, showcasing the success of commercial human spaceflight operations and advancing partnership between government and private space industries.

articles.title: Happy New Year on Mars
articles.description: 30 September 2026 marks the start of a new year on Mars. At exactly 10:16 CEST/08:16 UTC on Earth, the Red Planet begins a new orbit around our Sun.
articles.summary: Mars celebrates a new year in its orbital cycle, marking another fascinating milestone in humanity's ongoing exploration and study of the Red Planet's climate and seasons.

articles.title: Win a trip to ESA to witness BepiColombo arrive at Mercury
articles.description:
Get ready to celebrate BepiColombo’s arrival at Mercury. Craft a welcoming message that could be a drawing, song, poem or any other art form and stand a chance to win a trip to mission control!

articles.summary: The public is invited to participate in welcoming BepiColombo to Mercury, celebrating the European-Japanese mission's historic arrival at the solar system's innermost planet and engaging global participation in space exploration.
